- `brief_summary` (string | null): Brief summary, up to 1,000 characters (cut texts end with [truncated]); contact details removed.
- `eligibility` (object | null): detail=full only (null in summary): eligibility criteria.
- `arms` (array | null): detail=full only (null in summary): arms/groups, up to 20.
- `secondary_outcomes` (array | null): detail=full only (null in summary): secondary outcome measures, up to 15.
- `sites` (array | null): detail=full only (null in summary): study sites, up to 100. Organisation-level only: no contact persons, emails or phones.
- `source_url` (string | null): The trial's page on ClinicalTrials.gov.
- `data_processed_at` (string | null): When ClinicalTrials.gov last processed (posted) its dataset, from its /api/v2/version endpoint (dataTimestamp, no time zone given); null if that endpoint was unavailable.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When this Actor retrieved the record (ISO 8601, UTC).
- `attribution` (string): Required credit: source ClinicalTrials.gov, processing and retrieval dates, and the modifications made.
- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.

### Example input

```json
{ "nctIds": ["NCT05813925", "NCT04368728"] }
```

## Dutch Address Lookup API: BAG postcode, geocode & building data

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/dutch-address-lookup.html
Apify Store: coming soon
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/dutch-address-lookup
Price: $0.002 per resolved address

Validates and geocodes Dutch addresses against the official BAG register (via PDOK): postcode, BAG ids, WGS84 + RD coordinates, construction year, use, floor area and building status. Free text, postcode + house number (or range) or BAG ids; up to 100 per run. Unmatched inputs are free.

Example questions:

- Is 'Damrak 1 Amsterdam' a valid address? Give me its postcode, building year, use and floor area, with the source.

### Input fields

- `addresses` (array): Dutch addresses to check and geocode, one per line, as people write them: street + house number (+ letter or addition) + city, and/or postcode + house number, e.g. "Damrak 1 Amsterdam", "Dam 5B Amsterdam", "Damrak 18-1 Amsterdam", "Coolsingel 40, 3011AD Rotterdam", "1012LG 1". Up to 100 (together with bagIds); repeats are looked up once. One output row per address. Empty = use postcode or bagIds.
- `postcode` (string): A Dutch postcode, 4 digits + 2 letters, e.g. "1012JS" or "1012 JS". Alone it lists every address in that postcode (one row each, up to 100); with houseNumber it returns that address, with houseNumber + houseNumberTo every address in that range. Empty = not used.
- `houseNumber` (integer): House number within `postcode`, e.g. 1. Only used with postcode. Empty = all numbers in the postcode.
- `houseNumberTo` (integer): Last house number of a range starting at houseNumber, inclusive, e.g. 20 for 1-20. Needs postcode and houseNumber. Empty = only houseNumber.
- `houseNumberAddition` (string): House letter and/or addition for a single houseNumber, e.g. "B" (5B), "1" (18-1), "H" (8-H), "A2" (1A-2). Empty = all units at that number (one row each).
- `bagIds` (array): 16-digit BAG identifiers: nummeraanduiding (address, e.g. "0363200012113669"), verblijfsobject (unit, "0363010012111931"), ligplaats/standplaats (berth/pitch) or pand (building, "0363100012185508": building details only, no address). Up to 100 together with addresses. Empty = not used.
- `include` (array): Which sections to fill: any of "address" (street, postcode, city, municipality, province), "building" (construction year, use purposes, floor area, status, units in the building), "coordinates" (WGS84 + RD New), e.g. ["address", "coordinates"]. BAG ids are always returned. Default (or empty) = all three. Without "building" the run is faster; the price is the same.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `input` (string): The input as given: a free-text address, 'POSTCODE number(-to) addition' for postcode queries, or a BAG id.
- `input_type` (string): Which input this row answers: address (free text), postcode, or bag_id.
- `resolved` (boolean): true = one BAG address (or, for a pand id, one building) was found; only these rows are charged.
- `match_quality` (string): exact: every part of the input agrees with the BAG; probable: one address fits but part of the input differs or is missing (see warnings); ambiguous: several addresses fit (see candidates); not_found: no BAG address fits; invalid_input: not a valid BAG id; source_error: PDOK did not answer.
- `match_score` (number | null): PDOK Locatieserver relevance score for free-text matches (relative within one query, higher is better); null for postcode and BAG id lookups.
- `address` (object | null): The normalised BAG address. null when not resolved or 'address' is not in include.
- `bag_ids` (object): BAG identifiers of the address. Always present; values null when not resolved.
- `coordinates` (object | null): Point of the address (centroid of the unit). null when not resolved or 'coordinates' not in include.
- `building` (object | null): The BAG object and the building(s) it lies in. null when not resolved, 'building' not in include, or the BAG OGC API failed (see warnings).
- `candidates` (array): For ambiguous or not_found rows: up to 3 nearest BAG addresses (display_name, postcode, nummeraanduiding_id, score). Re-run with one of them, or its id in bagIds. Empty when resolved.
- `warnings` (array): Caveats and failures in plain words an agent can relay; the rest of the row is still valid.
- `source_url` (string | null): PDOK record the address (or, for a pand id, the building) was read from; null when not resolved.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When the row was made (ISO 8601, UTC).

### Example input

```json
{ "addresses": ["Damrak 1 Amsterdam", "Coolsingel 40, 3011AD Rotterdam", "1012LG 1", "Damrak 18-1 Amsterdam"] }
```

## PDF to JSON API: text, tables and metadata from a PDF URL

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/pdf-to-data.html
Apify Store: coming soon
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/pdf-to-data
Price: $0.0005 per page with text

PDF text, tables and metadata as clean JSON from 1-20 public PDF URLs or a base64 file: per-page markdown text in reading order, tables as rows with a header guess, title, author and dates. Processed in memory, never stored. Pay per page with text; scanned pages are flagged and free.

Example questions:

- Get the wage bracket table on page 14 of https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p15t.pdf as rows.

### Input fields

- `urls` (array): 1 to 20 public http(s) links to PDF files, e.g. ["https://www.sec.gov/files/form10-k.pdf"]. Each PDF gives one output row. Files up to 50 MB; links to private or local addresses are refused. Empty = use pdfBase64 instead.
- `pdfBase64` (string): Instead of (or besides) URLs: the PDF file itself, base64-encoded, optionally as a data: URI, e.g. "JVBERi0xLjQK...". Up to 50 MB decoded (Apify limits the whole input to a few MB, so use URLs for big files). Empty = none.
- `pages` (string): Which pages to read, 1-based, as ranges and single pages separated by commas, e.g. "1-5,10". Applies to every PDF; pages past the end are skipped with a warning. Empty = all pages (up to maxPages).
- `extract` (array): Any of text, tables, metadata, e.g. ["tables"]. Default (empty) = all three. Metadata alone costs one page per PDF.
- `maxPages` (integer): Most pages read per PDF, counted from the first selected page, e.g. 10. Default 50. You pay per page with text, so this caps the cost per PDF; a warning tells you how to request the rest.
- `outputFormat` (string): How page text is written: "markdown" marks headings with ## and writes detected tables as markdown tables; "text" gives plain paragraphs and tab-separated table rows. Default markdown. The tables field is the same in both.
- `timeoutSecs` (integer): Most seconds spent parsing one PDF, e.g. 60. Default 120. Pages are read until 3/4 of this time (later pages get a warning and are not charged); a PDF still parsing at the limit is stopped and returns an error row, not charged. Empty = 120.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `input_index` (integer): Position of this PDF in the input, 0-based: urls[input_index], or len(urls) for pdfBase64. Rows are written as each PDF finishes, so their order can differ from the input.
- `url` (string | null): The PDF URL as given in the input; null for pdfBase64.
- `final_url` (string | null): URL the PDF was finally downloaded from, after redirects; null for pdfBase64 or on error.
- `file_size_bytes` (integer | null): Size of the PDF file in bytes; null when it could not be downloaded.
- `page_count` (integer | null): Number of pages in the PDF; null on error.
- `pages_processed` (integer): Pages read in this run (after pages, maxPages and size limits).
- `pages_charged` (integer): Page events charged for this PDF: pages that had text (1 for a metadata-only request, 0 on error).
- `title` (string | null): Title from the PDF's document info; null if not set or metadata not requested.
- `author` (string | null): Author from the document info.
- `subject` (string | null): Subject from the document info.
- `creator` (string | null): Application that created the original document, e.g. Microsoft Word.
- `producer` (string | null): Application that wrote the PDF.
- `creation_date` (string | null): Creation date, ISO 8601 with the PDF's UTC offset when given, e.g. 2024-05-12T10:49:53-04:00.
- `modification_date` (string | null): Last modification date, ISO 8601.
- `pages` (array | null): One entry per processed page: {page (1-based), text}. text is markdown-ish (## headings, | tables |) or plain, in reading order; null for pages without a text layer. null when text was not requested.
- `tables` (array | null): Tables detected from aligned text: {page, header (first row when it looks like a header, else null), rows (arrays of cell strings, null = empty cell), n_cols}. null when tables were not requested.
- `warnings` (array): Things to know, e.g. scanned pages without text (OCR not supported, not charged) or pages left out by maxPages.
- `error` (string | null): Why this PDF failed (refused URL, download error, not a PDF, password-protected, unreadable, too complex: over the parse timeout or out of memory); null on success. Failed PDFs are not charged.
- `source_url` (string | null): Where the data came from (the input URL); null for pdfBase64.
- `retrieved_at` (string): UTC time the PDF was processed.

### Example input

```json
{ "urls": ["https://www.sec.gov/files/form10-k.pdf"], "pages": "1-5,10", "extract": ["text", "tables"] }
```

## Deduplicate & Merge Apify Datasets: remove duplicate items

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/dataset-dedup.html
Apify Store: coming soon
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/dataset-dedup
Price: $0.00015 per unique item written (duplicates are free)

Deduplicate and merge one or more Apify datasets (or a pasted JSON array): removes duplicate items by any fields (dot paths allowed) or by the whole item, keeping the first or last occurrence. Streams millions of items with constant memory. Use to clean repeated scraper runs before export.

Coverage: Works on the Apify datasets you pick in the input, or a pasted JSON array. For every distinct key the Actor keeps a 16-byte hash in memory, never the items: 10 million distinct keys need roughly 1-2 GB.

Example questions:

- Merge the results of my last three Google Maps runs and remove duplicate places by placeId.
- Deduplicate this list of leads by email and keep only name, email and website.
- Keep only the latest price per SKU from these two product datasets.

### Input fields

- `datasetIds` (array): Apify dataset IDs to merge, in this order, e.g. ["aBcD1234efGH5678i"]: a run's defaultDatasetId (Storage tab). Optional if you pass `items`.
- `items` (array): Items to deduplicate directly, as a JSON array of objects, e.g. [{"url": "https://example.com/a"}]. Processed before the datasets. Handy for small lists and quick tests.
- `fields` (array): Fields that form the duplicate key: items with equal values in all of them are duplicates. Dot paths work, e.g. ["url"] or ["address.city", "emails.0"]. Default [] = compare whole items. Items that have none of these fields are always kept.
- `keep` (string): "first" (default) keeps the first occurrence of each key; "last" keeps the last one and reads the datasets twice.
- `outputFields` (array): Top-level fields to keep in the output, e.g. ["url", "title"]. Empty = keep every field.

### Output fields

Items are copied unchanged from the input datasets (or reduced to outputFields).

### Example input

```json
{
  "datasetIds": ["aBcD1234efGH5678i", "jKlM9012noPQ3456r"],
  "fields": ["url"],
  "keep": "first",
  "outputFields": ["url", "title", "price"]
}
```

## Change Monitor: new, changed & removed items + Slack alerts

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/dataset-change-monitor.html
Apify Store: coming soon
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/dataset-change-monitor
Price: $0.001 per change reported

Run any scraper on a schedule and get only what changed: new, changed and removed items compared with the previous run, matched by your key fields (e.g. url). Optional Slack, Discord, Telegram, email or webhook alert per run. Add it as an integration to your scraper.

Example questions:

- Compare today's run of my shop scraper with the previous one by url and tell me which prices changed.

### Input fields

- `datasetId` (string): Apify dataset to compare with the previous run, e.g. "aBcD1234efGH5678i": usually your scraper run's default dataset. As an integration on your scraper, set it to "{{resource.defaultDatasetId}}" (see the README). Optional if you paste items.
- `items` (array): Items to check directly, as a JSON array of objects, e.g. [{"url": "https://jobs.example.com/1042", "salary_eur": 65000}]. Checked before the dataset. Pasted items are all reported as new on a monitor's first run (no silent baseline). Without a monitorName nothing is saved, so every run is a fresh try-out; give a monitorName and paste again with an edit to see a change.
- `monitorName` (string): Name of the saved state: one name = one watched list, e.g. "shop-prices". Runs with the same name are compared with each other; use a different name per scraper or task. Letters, digits, - and _. Empty = "default" with a datasetId; with only pasted items, empty = a try-out that saves nothing.
- `keyFields` (array): Fields that identify the same item in every run, e.g. ["url"] or ["placeId"]. Dot paths work: ["product.sku"]. Required unless you use whole-item comparison. Items without any key field are skipped.
- `compareWholeItem` (boolean): For datasets without an ID field: an item is identified by all its fields (minus ignored ones), so items are only reported as new or removed, never as changed. Default false.
- `ignoreFields` (array): Fields that change on every run and are never compared, as dot paths. Default: scrapedAt, scraped_at, crawledAt, retrieved_at, timestamp and #debug. Set [] to compare everything.
- `watchFields` (array): Only changes in these fields count, e.g. ["price", "stock", "offer.status"]. The output then also shows the old values (previous). Empty = every field except the ignored ones.
- `report` (array): Which changes become output rows (and are charged): new, changed and/or removed items. Removed is off by default, because a scraper run that stopped early would make many items look removed.
- `reportOnFirstRun` (boolean): The first run of a monitor only saves the baseline and reports nothing (free). Turn on to report every item as new on that first run (charged per item).
- `slackWebhookUrl` (string): Slack incoming webhook URL (https://hooks.slack.com/services/...). Secret input, stored encrypted.
- `discordWebhookUrl` (string): Discord channel webhook URL (https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...). Secret input, stored encrypted.
- `webhookUrl` (string): Any URL that receives a JSON POST with the counts, example rows and the link (Zapier, Make, n8n, your own API). Secret input, stored encrypted.
- `telegramBotToken` (string): Token of your Telegram bot from @BotFather. Needs the chat ID too. Secret input, stored encrypted.
- `telegramChatId` (string): Chat, group or channel ID the bot posts to, e.g. "123456789" or "@mychannel".
- `email` (string): Address(es) for an email alert, comma-separated. Sent by the public Actor apify/send-mail, which runs in your account (a few seconds of compute).
- `alertMaxItems` (integer): How many changes to list in the alert as examples (key values and what changed). Default 10.
- `alertWhenNoChanges` (boolean): Send the alert even when a run found no changes (a daily "all quiet"). Default false.

### Output fields

- `change_type` (string): new = key not seen in the previous run; changed = a compared field differs; removed = key missing from this run.
- `key` (object | null): The item's key field values, e.g. {"url": "https://..."}. null with whole-item comparison.
- `changed_fields` (array): changed rows: the fields that differ (top-level field names, or your watchFields paths). Empty for new and removed.
- `previous` (object | null): changed rows: the old values of the changed fields that were kept: all watchFields, else small values (text up to 200 characters, numbers, booleans; up to 20 fields and 400 characters per item). Long text, lists and objects are left out; a field that was missing before is null. null when no old value is known, and for new and removed rows.
- `item` (object | null): The current item, unchanged. For removed rows: the key values (the last known identity; with whole-item comparison, the removed item minus ignored fields).
- `monitor_name` (string): The monitorName of this run.
- `checked_at` (string): When this run started the comparison (UTC, ISO 8601).
- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version, "1".

### Example input

```json
{"datasetId": "<the run's dataset ID>", "monitorName": "shop", "keyFields": ["url"], "watchFields": ["price"]}
```

## Google Sheets Export: send any Apify dataset to a spreadsheet

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/sheets-export.html
Apify Store: coming soon
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/sheets-export
Price: $0.00015 per row exported

Export any Apify dataset to Google Sheets: replace a tab or append rows, with nested fields as columns and your header kept. Uses a Google service account key that never expires, so scheduled runs keep working; retries Google rate limits. Use to send scraper results to a spreadsheet.

Coverage: Any Apify dataset, written with your own Google service account (the sheet shared with it as Editor). Google allows 10 million cells per spreadsheet; rows are sent in batches of up to 5,000 rows or 2 MB.

Example questions:

- Put the results of my last Google Maps run into the 'Leads' tab of my spreadsheet, only name, phone and website.
- Replace the 'Daily' tab with today's scraper results.
- Append this week's new listings below the existing rows.

### Input fields

- `datasetId` (string, required): Apify dataset ID to export, e.g. "aBcD1234efGH5678i": usually the defaultDatasetId of a scraper run (Storage tab).
- `spreadsheetId` (string, required): Google spreadsheet ID: the part between /d/ and /edit in the sheet URL docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<ID>/edit, e.g. "1AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUvWxYz0123456789". The full sheet URL also works.
- `sheetName` (string): Name of the tab to write to, e.g. "Leads". Created if it doesn't exist. Leave empty to use the first tab (whatever it is called, e.g. "Sheet1" or "Blad1").
- `mode` (string): "replace" (default) clears the tab's values and writes the dataset; "append" adds rows below the existing data, keeps your header and adds any new columns on the right.
- `serviceAccountJson` (string, required): Full contents of a Google service account JSON key file (secret input, stored encrypted). Share the spreadsheet with that account's client_email as Editor first. See the README for the 2-minute setup.
- `fields` (array): Columns to export, in this order; nested fields use dots, e.g. ["name", "address.city", "phone"]. Empty = all fields.

### Output fields

The run writes no dataset rows. Its key-value store gets an OUTPUT record with spreadsheetUrl, sheetName, rowsWritten and columns. Nested objects become parent.child columns, arrays are written as JSON text, and values are never written as formulas.

### Example input

```json
{
  "datasetId": "aBcD1234efGH5678i",
  "spreadsheetId": "1AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUvWxYz0123456789",
  "sheetName": "Leads",
  "mode": "append",
  "serviceAccountJson": "{ \"type\": \"service_account\", ... }",
  "fields": ["name", "address.city", "phone", "website"]
}
```
